question: Which of the following structural modifications causes a morphine derivative to behave as an opioid (or opiate) receptor antagonist ?:

options.opa: A phenethyl group in the nitrogen and methylation of the hydroxyl in C-3.
options.opb: Oxidation of the hydroxyl in C-6 to ketone.
options.opc: An allyl group on nitrogen and a hydroxyl on C-14.
options.opd: Suppression of the double bond C7 = C8.

analysis: The presence of an allyl group on the nitrogen atom in morphine derivatives is known to convert the compound into an opioid receptor antagonist. This modification is characteristic of naloxone, a well-known opioid antagonist. Additionally, the presence of a hydroxyl group on C-14 is also associated with antagonist activity.
